Cord clamping studies report differences in blood volume, hemoglobin and anemia risk rather than a universal shortage, so the label reflects overstatement rather than a plain falsehood.

verdict.corrected_claim: Cutting the umbilical cord early (early cord clamping) deprives the newborn of some placental blood, which lowers its blood volume and iron stores and raises the risk of anemia; it does not guarantee that the baby will lack enough blood right after birth.
verdict.correction_reasoning: Based on general knowledge of the Cochrane reviews on delayed cord clamping and WHO/ACOG guidance; not verified against live sources in this offline session.
verdict.claim: If the umbilical cord is cut early, the baby will not have enough blood right after birth.

verdict.explanation: Masks can trap some exhaled CO2 and slightly raise the amount a wearer rebreathes, but in healthy people this stays small and does not cause carbon dioxide intoxication (hypercapnia). chosen_claim: The Obama-Biden administration secretly launched a surveillance operation on the Trump campaign.

verdict.label: Conflicting Evidence/Cherrypicking
verdict.confidence_reasoning: No web access, so this rests on my own knowledge of the 2016-2019 record as of the claim date. The core facts (FBI Crossfire Hurricane, FISA warrants on Carter Page, the confidential human source contacting Trump advisers, and the December 2019 DOJ Inspector General report on FISA errors) are well documented. The sticking point is the wording "secretly launched a surveillance operation on the Trump campaign," which is contested. I did not verify exact quotes, so I cite no sources.
verdict.explanation: The FBI's Crossfire Hurricane investigation, opened in July 2016 under the Obama administration, did involve a confidential source who contacted Trump campaign advisers, and FISA surveillance of former adviser Carter Page was obtained. However, the DOJ Inspector General (Dec 2019) found the investigation was opened on a predicated basis and did not find documentary evidence of political bias in opening it, while documenting serious FISA application errors. Calling it a secret Obama-Biden surveillance operation on the campaign as a whole is a politically loaded framing that omits this context.
verdict.corrected_claim: In 2016 the FBI, under the Obama administration, opened a counterintelligence investigation (Crossfire Hurricane) into possible links between Trump campaign associates and Russia. It used a confidential human source and obtained FISA warrants targeting former campaign adviser Carter Page. A DOJ Inspector General review found the investigation was opened on a predicated basis but identified significant errors and omissions in the FISA applications.
verdict.correction_reasoning: Based on my knowledge of the DOJ OIG report (December 2019) and the public record of Crossfire Hurricane and the Page FISA warrants. Not verified against live sources in this session.
verdict.claim: The Obama-Biden administration secretly launched a surveillance operation on the Trump campaign.

ocr_text: Covid 19 Will Go Away If You Stop Getting Tested, It's Just The Elderly Dying and People Are Being Intentionally Infected
extracted: COVID-19 will go away if people stop getting tested.
COVID-19 deaths are occurring only among the elderly.
People are being intentionally infected with COVID-19.
chosen_claim: COVID-19 will go away if people stop getting tested.

verdict.label: Refuted
verdict.confidence_reasoning: The claim is a basic causal error that is well established in public health. Testing only detects infections; it does not cause or prevent them. I did not have web access to pull and quote a specific source, so I am relying on my own knowledge of how testing and epidemics work rather than on cited documents, which keeps confidence below the level I would give with multiple retrieved sources.
verdict.explanation: Testing identifies existing infections and does not change how many people are infected or how the virus spreads. Stopping testing would reduce reported case counts, which is a measurement effect, but infections would continue to circulate unseen. The virus would not disappear because fewer people were tested.
verdict.corrected_claim: Stopping COVID-19 testing would lower reported case numbers, but it would not make the virus go away; infections would continue to spread undetected.
verdict.correction_reasoning: This follows directly from how diagnostic testing works: tests detect infection and do not affect transmission. Reduced testing only reduces detection of cases.
verdict.claim: COVID-19 will go away if people stop getting tested.

verdict.label: Supported
verdict.confidence_reasoning: I had no web access, so this rests on my recollection of CDC abortion surveillance figures (rate per 1,000 women aged 15-44), not on sources I could check. The approximate figures I recall point the same way: roughly 11% decline under Reagan (1981-1988), about 20% under Clinton (1993-2001), and about 30% or more under Obama (2009-2016). Under Bush I and Bush II the declines were small or flat, and Trump's term was short and fairly flat. I am fairly confident in the direction but not in the exact numbers, and I have no direct quotes to cite.
verdict.explanation: As I recall the CDC rate series, abortion rates fell by a larger percentage and at a faster pace during Democratic administrations (Clinton and Obama) than during Republican ones (Reagan, Bush I, Bush II). The claim is therefore supported as a descriptive comparison. It is still open to the objection that presidents have limited direct control over abortion rates, so the framing implies more causal credit than the data supports.
verdict.claim: The rate of abortions has fallen more precipitously under Democratic presidential administrations than under Republican presidential administrations.

verdict.correction_reasoning: Based on general knowledge of respirator and mask filtration performance and the droplet-based transmission understanding in 2020. The exact degree of cloth-mask efficacy was still debated then, so the correction avoids specific numbers for cloth masks.

verdict.correction_reasoning: The corrected version reflects the widely cited CDC safety guidance on seasonal flu vaccines as of 2020. Based on memory, not a live check.

verdict.corrected_claim: Masks, particularly N95 and surgical masks and to a lesser extent well-made cloth masks, reduce the emission and inhalation of respiratory droplets and aerosols that can carry SARS-CoV-2, though effectiveness depends on mask type and fit.

extracted: A US voter can legally vote four times because they received four vote-by-mail forms.

verdict.label: Refuted
verdict.confidence_reasoning: The claim is a basic point of US election law, and I am confident in the general rule: one eligible voter may cast one ballot per election, and casting more than one is a crime. I could not check sources live (no web access here), and I cite none, so my confidence rests on established legal knowledge rather than a retrieved document. Some uncertainty remains about the specific state rules in place in September 2020.
verdict.explanation: Receiving more than one mail-in ballot does not make it legal to vote more than once. Each eligible voter may cast only one valid ballot per election, and voting twice is a felony under federal and state law. Extra ballots usually come from duplicate registrations, address errors, or mailing mistakes, and election officials are expected to cancel the duplicates.
verdict.corrected_claim: A US voter who receives multiple mail-in ballots may legally cast only one of them. Voting more than once in the same election is illegal, and extra ballots are typically cancelled by election officials.
verdict.correction_reasoning: Single-vote-per-election is a long-standing and uncontested rule across US states, and double voting is prosecuted as a crime. The exact handling of duplicate ballots varies by state, so the wording stays general.
verdict.claim: A US voter can legally vote four times because they received four vote-by-mail forms.

Nigerian pump prices were roughly N125 to N162 per litre in 2020, and Saudi 91-octane was about 1.37 SAR per litre (about $0.36). Whether Nigeria was dearer depends on the exchange rate used (official vs parallel), the fuel grade, and the month, so the answer is unclear. I could not confirm the exact figures.

At the official exchange rate, Nigeria's petrol price of about N162/L (roughly $0.42/L) was at or above Saudi 91-octane (roughly $0.36/L), which would support the claim. At the parallel-market rate or during the lower April 2020 pump price (about N125/L), Nigerian petrol was cheaper in dollar terms, which would contradict it. The claim therefore needs a specific date, grade and exchange rate to be judged.
verdict.corrected_claim: In 2020, Nigerian petrol's dollar price was close to Saudi Arabia's: at the official exchange rate, Nigeria's higher pump prices (about N162/L) were roughly equal to or above Saudi 91-octane, but Nigeria was cheaper at lower prices or parallel-market rates.
verdict.correction_reasoning: Based on approximate recall of 2020 pump prices, exchange rates and Saudi fuel prices, not on verified sources. The exact figures and timing are uncertain.
verdict.claim: Fuel in Nigeria in 2020 was not cheaper than fuel in Saudi Arabia.

ocr_text: Because of a so-called trade war with China, America lost 300,000 manufacturing jobs.
extracted: America lost 300,000 manufacturing jobs.
America's loss of manufacturing jobs was caused by a trade war with China.
chosen_claim: America's loss of manufacturing jobs was caused by a trade war with China.

verdict.label: Refuted
verdict.confidence_reasoning: The claim's timing and causal story conflict with well-established economic research and BLS employment data that I know well. I had no web access, so I could not pull and quote sources for this check, and I am relying on memory. The main uncertainty is how much weight the other drivers, such as automation, deserve. That affects the size of the China effect, not the verdict that a 2018 trade war did not cause the earlier losses.
verdict.explanation: US manufacturing employment peaked around 1979 and fell steadily for decades. The sharpest losses came in the 2000s, after China joined the WTO in 2001, when a surge of Chinese imports displaced US production; economists such as Autor, Dorn and Hanson (the "China shock" research) attribute roughly 2 million lost jobs to this. The tariff trade war started in 2018, after most of that decline had already happened, and manufacturing jobs were roughly flat or slightly up during the tariff period before the COVID drop. So the trade war did not cause the job losses; the earlier import competition from China, along with automation, did.
verdict.corrected_claim: America's manufacturing job losses were driven mainly by surging Chinese import competition after China joined the WTO in 2001, along with automation and other factors; the 2018–2019 tariff trade war came after most of those losses.
verdict.correction_reasoning: This follows from the timing of the 2018 tariffs against the long decline in manufacturing employment, and from the China-shock literature (Autor, Dorn & Hanson). I did not verify it against live sources.
verdict.claim: America's loss of manufacturing jobs was caused by a trade war with China.

People for whom coverage was unaffordable were generally exempt, and the penalty was not $10,000.
verdict.correction_reasoning: The penalty structure (percentage of income or flat dollar amount, $695 per adult in 2016, affordability exemption) is well documented in IRS and KFF materials from that period, but I could not check them live here.

verdict.corrected_claim: Supreme Court nominees have been nominated and confirmed during a presidential election year while the campaign was underway, for example Melville Fuller in 1888 and John Hessin Clarke in July 1916. The claim that this has never happened is false.
verdict.correction_reasoning: Both examples are well-known from the historical record on Supreme Court confirmations, but I could not verify exact dates offline. Fuller's confirmation in 1888 is somewhat less clearly "during the election" than Clarke's in 1916.
verdict.claim: No Supreme Court nominee has ever been nominated and confirmed while a presidential election was already underway.

verdict.confidence_reasoning: The claim is a specific factual assertion about UPSC rules, which I know well from background knowledge. UPSC sets one qualifying standard for all candidates in the same category, with separate cut-offs only for reserved categories (SC, ST, OBC, EWS, PwBD) and relaxations based on those categories. I could not check sources live in this offline session, so confidence is high but not maximal, and I cite no URLs.
verdict.explanation: UPSC civil services exams have no religion-based marks relaxation or lower cut-off for Muslim candidates. Qualifying is decided by merit, with cut-offs varying by reservation category (SC, ST, OBC, EWS) and by disability, not by religion. The claim, which circulated in the 2020 Sudarshan News "UPSC jihad" programme, is therefore false.
verdict.corrected_claim: UPSC civil services candidates are not given lower qualifying marks because they are Muslim. Cut-offs differ only by reservation category (such as SC, ST, OBC, EWS) and disability status, and apply the same standard to all candidates within a category regardless of religion.
verdict.correction_reasoning: This reflects UPSC's published reservation framework, where relaxations are tied to category and disability, not religion. Religion is not a criterion for relaxation in the exam.
verdict.claim: Muslim candidates can qualify for the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) civil services exam with lower marks than other candidates.
